1: ElastiCache keeps hot data in memory, so it lowers latency and raises throughput for read-heavy workloads and can store the results of expensive computations so compute-intensive applications do not repeat them. It has no effect on S3 PUT speed, CodeDeploy deployment latency or CodeCommit branch merges, which are unrelated to caching.
2: ElastiCache (Redis/Memcached), DynamoDB and S3 all store and retrieve data by a unique key, so they are key/value stores. SNS is a pub/sub notification service and SWF is a workflow coordination service, so neither is a data store.
3: For a Lambda function behind an ALB, multi-value headers are not delivered by default. You must enable the multi-value headers attribute on the ALB target group so headers and query parameters arrive as arrays. Account placement, a 1 MB body limit, or response formatting do not turn on this feature.
4: To keep the cache and database strongly consistent, write to the backend first and then invalidate the cache entry. The next read repopulates the cache from the fresh data and stays fast. Writing to the cache first or waiting for expiry leaves stale or inconsistent prices, and a dual write can leave the two out of sync if one write fails.
5: Data is encrypted in transit either by using SSL/TLS (HTTPS) endpoints or by encrypting on the client before upload, so client-side encryption with a KMS key and SSL both qualify. Server-side encryption options only protect data at rest after it reaches S3. A VPN plus VPC endpoint is not the intended answer here.
6: SSE-KMS encrypts on the S3 side, so the application does not change or slow down, and every use of the KMS key is logged in AWS CloudTrail, which gives the audit trail. SSE-S3 has no per-use key audit. Client-side encryption adds work and processing in the application, which affects performance.
7: Cross-account IAM roles in Accounts B and C that trust Account A let the application call STS AssumeRole and get short-lived credentials, with no long-term secrets. Long-lived IAM user access keys are less secure, S3 replication is not a way to call services, and per-account application deployments add needless complexity.
8: CodeDeploy can deploy a revision only from S3 or GitHub (and similar supported sources), not from on-premises local storage. So upload the zip/tar bundle to S3 and reference it in the deployment. CodeCommit does not automatically deploy and CodeBuild builds artifacts rather than deploying to EC2.
9: Encrypted EBS volumes encrypt data at rest on the volume and in transit between the instance and volume, using hardware offload with minimal performance impact. Custom algorithms in the app burn CPU, writing everything to S3 changes the architecture, and ephemeral instance store disks are not the persistent EBS storage the app uses.
10: CloudFront caches the images at edge locations close to users, which cuts load on the EC2 instances and S3 and improves latency globally. ElastiCache suits application data, not serving static image files to browsers. S3 request limits are per prefix and are not raised by a support ticket.
11: To encrypt the file before upload, the function calls KMS GenerateDataKey to get a plaintext data key plus an encrypted copy, encrypts the 3 MB file locally with the plaintext key (envelope encryption) and uploads the ciphertext. Encrypt via KMS directly only handles up to 4 KB, and S3-managed keys are not used with GenerateDataKey.
12: Browsers block cross-origin font requests unless the server returns CORS headers. Configuring a CORS configuration on the cdfonts bucket that allows the website origin fixes this. Versioning, a public-access policy or a Content-MD5 header do not add the needed Access-Control-Allow-Origin response.
13: To redeploy an existing SAM application you first run sam build to compile the functions and dependencies into deployable artifacts, then sam deploy to package and deploy through CloudFormation. sam init only creates a new project, sam validate only checks the template, and sam publish sends the app to the Serverless Application Repository.
14: Rolling with additional batch launches an extra batch of new instances first, so full capacity is kept throughout the deployment, and it still updates the existing instances in place. Plain Rolling reduces capacity by a batch, All at once takes the app down, and Immutable launches entirely new instances instead of using existing ones.
15: The instance metadata service at 169.254.169.254 exposes instance details such as the public IPv4 address (under meta-data/public-ipv4). User data holds the launch script, not the IP address. Running ifconfig or ipconfig shows only the private address because the public IP is NATed outside the instance.
16: API Gateway caching is billed per hour for the cache size, so the cost is driven by keeping the 237 GB cache running in every stage. Enabling the cache for development and test only when needed removes most of that cost. Splitting stages into separate gateways or accounts does not change the cache cost.
17: A read replica offloads read queries from the primary, so the application should use a separate connection string pointing at the RDS read replica for reads. Multi-AZ is for high availability and its standby does not serve reads, retries with vertical scaling do not improve read throughput, and a replica on EC2 is not an RDS read replica.
18: Processing data as it arrives is an event-driven pattern, for example DynamoDB Streams triggering Lambda on each change. A scheduled nightly batch is the schedule-driven pattern that causes the delay. Fan-out and client-server driven are not patterns for near-real-time processing of table changes.
19: Throttling comes from exceeding provisioned throughput. Retrying with exponential backoff spreads requests out, and switching the table to on-demand capacity removes the need to manage write capacity. Increasing RCUs does not help writes, a larger EC2 instance does not change DynamoDB limits, and retrying faster makes throttling worse.
20: SSE-KMS lets AWS manage the encryption infrastructure while the company controls the customer managed KMS key, with key policies, rotation and audit through CloudTrail. SSE-S3 gives no key control, SSE-C forces the company to manage and supply keys on every request, and client-side encryption puts the work in-house.
21: With KCL, each shard is processed by exactly one worker at a time, so the maximum number of useful workers equals the number of open shards. After resharding from 4 to 6 shards, up to 6 EC2 instances can process data in parallel. More instances than shards would sit idle.
22: Amazon Cognito (Cognito Sync / AppSync-style data sync with identity pools) stores user profile data and syncs it across a user's devices without writing a backend. Lambda, S3 and DynamoDB could store data but would require building and securing a custom backend and authentication.
23: Elastic Beanstalk accepts a .zip (or .war) source bundle, not .tar. You can upload and deploy the zip in the console, or create an application version from the zip with the CLI and update the environment with the CLI. The .tar options use an unsupported format, and rebuilding the environment is not how you deploy a new version.
24: The /tmp directory (512 MB, in newer versions configurable) persists across invocations in the same warm execution environment, so caching the 50 MB file there avoids downloading it every time. A longer timeout does not speed anything up, a load balancer does not help Lambda, and S3 still requires a download per invocation.
25: A global secondary index that projects only the few attributes the application needs lets queries read small items, which uses less read capacity than reading the large base items. Batching writes, exponential backoff or a load balancer in front of DynamoDB do not reduce the size of items read.
26: API Gateway uses a mapping template (Velocity template) in the integration request to transform query string parameters into the JSON event the Lambda function expects. Request validation only checks inputs, the function ARN just identifies the target, and changing the integration type does not map parameters.
27: A separate IAM user for each developer with their own access keys is the simple way to give local machines AWS access, and each key is individually auditable and revocable. A shared user and key is insecure, assuming a role still needs initial credentials, and Cognito federation is far more complex than needed.
28: A strongly consistent read consumes one read capacity unit per 4 KB, while an eventually consistent read consumes half of that. So strongly consistent reads use more throughput, twice as much as eventually consistent reads. It is not variable based on activity.
29: You deploy a new version by uploading the new application bundle as an application version and deploying it to the environment, either in the console or with eb deploy. eb init only configures the project, terminating and recreating the environment is disruptive, and .ebextensions customize the environment, not deploy versions.
30: Option A restricts access with dynamodb:LeadingKeys equal to the caller's web identity user_id, so a user can only touch their own item, and dynamodb:Attributes limits the writable attribute to user_name. Option B reverses the roles, matching on user_name as the key and allowing user_id, which would let users change the wrong data.
31: Use an alias that points to the live version and shift traffic gradually with weighted alias routing, such as 10 percent to the new version. If errors rise, move all traffic back to the previous version. Only a small share of users is affected, unlike flipping the alias fully to the new version at once. Using a raw version ARN or a three-alias router is more complex.
32: Each component has different scaling needs, so deploy them as separate Elastic Beanstalk environments: a web server environment for HTTP and a worker environment for background tasks (for example reading from SQS). A single environment scales everything together, so the components could not scale independently.
33: CloudFormation change sets let you preview how proposed template changes would affect running resources, such as which are modified or replaced, before you execute them. Stack policies only prevent updates to resources, and the Metadata and Resources sections just describe the template and do not show impact.
34: Lambda versions and aliases give a stable alias ARN that API Gateway targets. New code is published as a new version and the alias is repointed, so API Gateway never needs updating. Different functions per endpoint, stage changes or tags would still require reconfiguring API Gateway.
35: A bucket policy that denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false blocks all plain HTTP access and forces HTTPS. An Allow on SecureTransport true does not block other access paths, and certificates or HTTPS redirects on the EC2 instances do not control how requests reach S3.
36: A REST endpoint with a path like /status/customerID can be served by API Gateway plus Lambda, or by an ELB with EC2 instances running a web server. SQS/SNS are messaging services, ElastiCache/Elasticsearch are data stores, and S3 with CloudFront serves static content, none of which implement a dynamic REST API.
37: Lambda provides ephemeral /tmp storage (512 MB by default), local to the execution environment and fast, which fits small temporary files that are modified repeatedly and not needed later. EFS, EBS and S3 add latency and cost, and EBS cannot be attached to Lambda.
38: Cache-aside (lazy loading) with ElastiCache stores user profiles only when they are requested, which keeps the cache small and reduces database reads. A dedicated EC2 NoSQL or RDS instance as a cache adds operational overhead, and write-through caches every write, including data that is never read.
39: Elastic Beanstalk handles provisioning, load balancing and Auto Scaling for you, so the company only supplies website code, which matches handling everything except development. VM Import and Lightsail leave you managing infrastructure, and S3 with CloudFront serves only static content, not a dynamic website.
40: The Lambda context object provides the request ID (aws_request_id) unique to each invocation. Writing logs to the console (stdout) sends them to CloudWatch Logs, where each line can be tied to that invocation. The event object holds input data, not the request ID, and Lambda cannot persist files to log to.
41: The EC2 instance role in Account B needs permission to call sts:AssumeRole on the AccessPII role, and the code must call AssumeRole to get temporary credentials that are then used to access the DynamoDB table in Account A. Giving the instance role direct table access does not work cross-account, and GetSessionToken does not switch roles.
42: AWS X-Ray tracing on the Lambda function, with the SDK instrumenting downstream calls, shows a trace with timing for each DynamoDB call and identifies bottlenecks. DynamoDB is not an event source for this purpose, ALBs do not sit in front of DynamoDB, and limiting concurrency does not reveal timing.
43: A read replica takes over the read traffic, so daily write load on the primary no longer slows reads for users. Multi-AZ is only for failover and its standby is not readable, ElastiCache does not buffer writes, and moving to DynamoDB is a heavy redesign that does not solve the issue.
44: DynamoDB TransactWriteItems groups multiple writes across items into one all-or-nothing ACID transaction. BatchWriteItem is not atomic and there is no table-level setting to enable transactions. An SQS FIFO queue or an Aurora transaction table adds unneeded complexity and does not provide atomic DynamoDB updates.
45: Call PutMetricData to publish a custom metric, and give the EC2 instance an IAM role with the needed permission so credentials are provided securely and automatically. Embedding credentials is insecure, and routing through S3 or Kinesis plus Lambda is needlessly complicated.
46: SQS messages are limited to 256 KB, so larger payloads are stored in S3 and a pointer is sent in the message. The SQS Extended Client Library for Java does this automatically for payloads up to 2 GB. EBS and EFS cannot be used this way, and the CLI does not handle large payload offloading.
47: Publish the thread count as a custom CloudWatch metric with PutMetricData, then graph it on a CloudWatch dashboard or metrics view. This is the simplest graphical monitoring. X-Ray is for request tracing, and building graphs from S3 and Kinesis or DynamoDB and CloudFront is not a monitoring solution.
48: Initializing the database connection outside the handler lets warm invocations reuse it, saving connection time, and packaging only required modules shrinks the deployment package so cold starts are faster. Both cost nothing extra. Switching to DynamoDB is a redesign, and custom pooling or local caching is unreliable in Lambda.
49: Third-party API errors in your code are not an AWS metric, so you publish a custom CloudWatch metric for the failures, create an alarm on a threshold and have it notify via SNS. There is no built-in CloudWatch API-error metric for this, and SES is for email sending rather than alarm notifications.
50: CodePipeline provides a manual approval action that you add to a stage before the deployment stage, and the pipeline pauses until someone approves or rejects (optionally with an SNS notification). Multiple pipelines or disabling stages or transitions are workarounds, not the built-in approval mechanism.
51: ElastiCache Redis in cluster mode (with replicas and Multi-AZ) provides sharding, replication and automatic failover and persistence options, so expensive-to-recreate data survives failures. Memcached has no replication or persistence, a self-managed Redis on EC2 needs manual HA, and Redshift is a data warehouse, not a cache.
52: Image conversion is memory and CPU intensive, and Lambda allocates CPU in proportion to memory. A default or low memory setting makes it run far slower than on a 1 GB instance, so it likely times out or runs out of memory before copying. The 15-minute limit is not hit at 500 seconds on the EC2 test, and the Java runtime and bucket layout are fine.
53: Kinesis Data Streams supports server-side encryption with KMS keys, which encrypts data at rest in the stream. SSL protects data in transit only, the Kinesis Client Library is for consuming records, and encrypting with Lambda after the data is stored does not make it encrypted at rest in the stream.
54: Amazon Cognito is scalable and low-cost, supports user sign-up and sign-in, and can federate with a SAML 2.0 identity provider through identity pools or user pools. Lambda and EC2 would require building the identity system yourself, and IAM is not meant for mobile app end users.
55: Auto Scaling policies need a CloudWatch metric, and concurrent users is an application-level value that AWS does not publish. Publish it as a custom CloudWatch metric and scale on it. NetworkIn is only a proxy, SNS only notifies, and CloudFront does not scale instances.
56: The Serverless Application Model extends CloudFormation to define Lambda, API Gateway and DynamoDB concisely and packages dependencies, and CloudFormation provides rollback on failed deployments. Raw API calls or bash scripts have no built-in rollback, and plain CloudFormation is more verbose than SAM for serverless.
57: Fine-grained access control uses IAM policy conditions such as dynamodb:LeadingKeys, restricting each user to items whose partition key matches their identity. Encrypting per user, staging via SQS, or filtering client-side still lets users reach other users' data or are impractical.
58: Cognito identity pools can issue temporary AWS credentials to unauthenticated (guest) identities with a limited IAM role, as well as authenticated users. STS alone needs an initial credential, Directory Service is for directories, and SAML integration requires an authenticated identity provider.
59: The template uses a local path to the function code, so aws cloudformation package uploads the code to S3 and outputs a new template with the S3 location, which aws cloudformation deploy can then deploy. There is no cloudformation compile, Lambda zip command with the template, or serverless create-package command.
60: Lambda has a hard limit on unzipped deployment package size (250 MB) that cannot be raised, so the fix is to split the function into smaller functions, or move dependencies into layers or a container image. Compression tricks do not reduce the unzipped size, and support cannot raise this limit.
61: Lambda functions are stateless and the local filesystem is not shared between execution environments, so session data must be kept in an external store such as DynamoDB. SQS is a queue not meant for lookups, and local files or SQLite on the filesystem are lost or not shared across invocations.
62: ProvisionedThroughputExceeded errors during short bursts are handled by retrying with exponential backoff, which spreads the retries until capacity is available. Immediate retries add more load, a GSI does not add base table capacity, and UpdateItem edits item data, not table throughput.
63: Rolling with additional batch launches a new batch first so full capacity is kept during the update, and then updates existing instances, which costs less than Immutable, which launches a full second set of instances. Rolling reduces capacity and All at once causes downtime.
64: Clients created outside the handler are initialized once per execution environment and reused by later warm invocations, which reuses connections and lowers latency. Creating them inside the handler recreates the client on every call, which wastes time. Style and error handling are not the benefit.
65: AWS Step Functions lets you define the workflow as a state machine with built-in state management, retries and error handling, replacing brittle custom coordination code between Lambda functions. Data Pipeline, EMR and SNS with SQS are not workflow orchestrators for Lambda.
66: ECS task roles let each task definition reference its own IAM role, so each of the four services gets only its own least-privilege permissions. An instance profile would give all containers the same combined permissions, and ECS services and clusters do not reference IAM roles or groups in the way described.
67: Step Functions standard workflows can run for up to a year, support parallel states to call vendors concurrently and join the results, and need little code. Lambda alone has a 15-minute limit, SQS with worker instances means more to manage, and CloudWatch Events does not orchestrate state.
68: DynamoDB TTL deletes expired items automatically at no extra write cost. Store an expiry time (epoch seconds, a Number attribute) set to 48 hours after creation and enable TTL on that attribute. Scripts, scans and scheduled jobs consume read and write capacity and compute and cost more.
69: ThrottlingException is a transient rate limit, so the first best practice is to retry with exponential backoff (the AWS SDKs do this by default). Removing the API call or using the CLI does not address throttling, and a support limit increase is not the first step.
70: Kinesis Data Streams lets multiple consumers read the same records concurrently and cost-effectively at high volume, with replay. SNS to SQS fan-out needs a queue per consumer and costs more at millions of events, and Firehose delivers to a destination rather than serving multiple custom consumers.
71: CodeDeploy requires the appspec.yml file in the root of the application source directory structure (the revision bundle). It is not located in a bin folder, in S3 separately, or with configuration files; the revision bundle itself is what goes to S3.
72: Kinesis Data Firehose ingests high-throughput streaming data from many sources and loads it directly into S3 with no consumers to manage. S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads but does not ingest streaming data, and SQS and SNS are messaging services that do not store to S3.
73: A Lambda layer holds the external libraries once, so they are not installed at runtime on each invocation, which saves compute time, and it can be shared across functions. Installing at the start of the function wastes time every cold start, and fetching from S3 also costs time.
74: Parallel scans split the table into segments processed concurrently, which speeds up the full scan, and limiting the rate leaves capacity for normal workloads. Sequential scans are slower, raising RCUs costs more, and eventual consistency only reduces cost per read, not the scan structure.
75: Note: the marked answer may be wrong. CloudFront is a correct choice because it caches static objects at the edge and lowers load on S3, but randomizing key prefixes is outdated advice. S3 now scales to at least 5,500 GET requests per second per prefix, so 300 GET/s needs no prefix randomization.
76: API Gateway can expose a SOAP service as a REST API by using mapping templates in the integration request to transform the incoming JSON into the XML SOAP envelope. Passing JSON directly through an ALB would not be understood by the SOAP service, and the client is not required to send XML.
77: SSE-KMS makes S3 call KMS to generate and decrypt data keys for each object, and KMS has a per-account request quota. At tens of thousands of uploads per second, the KMS API limit is hit, causing throttling and latency. S3 does not throttle encryption by CMK and aliases are optional.
78: Rolling deployment updates the existing instances in batches, so it keeps access logs on those instances and minimizes the outage by updating a batch at a time. All at once causes an outage, and Immutable and Rolling with additional batch launch new instances.
79: Kinesis guarantees ordering of records within each shard only. A Lambda consumer receives records from a shard in the exact order they were put into the shard (FIFO), and there is no ordering across the 4 shards. It is not LIFO and consumers cannot choose the order.
80: A bucket policy can deny s3:PutObject requests that lack the x-amz-server-side-encryption header, which enforces encryption on upload. Notifications or CloudWatch rules only detect unencrypted objects after the fact, and denying requests that include the header would block encrypted uploads.
81: In an SQS FIFO queue, messages with the same MessageGroupId are processed in order, so giving each sender a unique MessageGroupId preserves each sender's order. Unique IDs per message would put every message in its own group with no ordering, and deduplication IDs only prevent duplicates.
82: Amazon Cognito provides sign-in and user directory features for web and mobile apps, and can store user profile data and sync preferences across devices and platforms. KMS manages keys, Directory Service is for AD, and IAM users are not intended for end users of an app.
83: Lambda environment variables let the same deployment package get environment-specific values, such as database endpoints, through configuration for each environment. Hardcoding resources ties code to one environment, and tags or separate function code per environment add maintenance.
84: A cross-account IAM role that users assume via sts:AssumeRole returns temporary, short-lived credentials, which is the most secure approach. Mailing access keys or adding SSH keys is insecure, and Cognito user pools do not provide IAM credentials for another account.
85: For X-Ray on EC2, you install and run the X-Ray daemon, which relays trace segments to the X-Ray service, and instrument the application code with the X-Ray SDK. The SDK alone cannot send data without the daemon, and the daemon does not send to CloudWatch Events.
86: Use an IAM role with PutMetricData permission and launch instances with it through the launch configuration (instance profile). Credentials are temporary and rotated automatically with nothing stored. IAM user keys in a repo or in user data are insecure, and CloudWatch has no resource policy for instances.
87: A partition key should have many distinct values spread evenly across requests. reviewID is a unique UUID per record, so it distributes items uniformly across partitions. starRating has only five values, and productID and comment can have uneven or hot access patterns.
88: Note: the marked answer may be wrong. The generic approach is IAM policy variables: replace TeamMemberX in the resource ARN with ${aws:username}, which is substituted at request time so one policy serves all ten members. A condition element could not rewrite the resource path, and principal or resource alone are not the mechanism.
89: SSE with AWS KMS uses a managed service while letting the company use its own customer managed master key, with control over key policies and audit through CloudTrail. SSE-S3 uses keys managed by S3 and client-side encryption is not a managed service.
90: You can test permissions without side effects by running the action with --dry-run, which checks authorization, and by validating the role's policies with the IAM policy simulator. Querying IAM groups, metadata, or STS tokens does not verify access to Kinesis.
91: The pipeline can take code from CodeCommit, run unit tests with CodePipeline stages (CodeBuild), and failures can trigger notifications through Amazon SNS. SES is for email sending and not a pipeline notification mechanism. Note that CloudWatch Events/EventBridge also route to SNS, but SNS delivers the notification.
92: The default visibility timeout is 30 seconds, shorter than the 40 seconds of processing, so another consumer could get the message. Extend it with ChangeMessageVisibility and delete the message with DeleteMessage after processing. Decreasing the timeout makes duplicates more likely, and deleting the queue is destructive.
93: Amazon Cognito user pools support MFA (SMS or TOTP) for application end users. IAM with MFA is for AWS console and API users, Directory Service is not an app MFA solution by itself, and building MFA with DynamoDB and SNS is custom work.
94: One RCU gives one strongly consistent 4 KB read per second or two eventually consistent ones. 5 RCUs eventually consistent on 4 KB items is 10 reads (40 KB per second). 15 RCUs on 1 KB items is 30 reads (30 KB/s) eventually consistent, 15 strongly consistent, and 5 strongly consistent would be less, so option A gives the highest throughput.
95: Server access logging writes log objects to the same bucket, and each log write is itself a request that is logged, creating a loop that causes exponential growth. Log to a different bucket. Versioning, replication or lifecycle transitions would not grow a 100 KB upload to 50 GB.
96: An ECS task IAM role gives containers temporary credentials via the container credential provider, with permissions scoped to the task and no keys to manage. Environment variables or credential files with access keys are long-lived secrets, and manual AssumeRole code is unneeded.
97: The CodeBuild project build history shows logs for each phase, so the failed phase in the last build output reveals the compilation error. Adding CloudWatch steps or X-Ray is unneeded, as CodeBuild already logs, and re-running locally is not equivalent to the build environment.
98: For in-place deployments the hook order is ApplicationStop, BeforeInstall, then the install step, AfterInstall, ApplicationStart and ValidateService. So Application Stop comes first, then Before Install, After Install and Application Start. The other options put the hooks in the wrong order.
99: The encoded authorization failure message returned by some EC2 errors is decoded with the AWS STS DecodeAuthorizationMessage API, which requires the sts:DecodeAuthorizationMessage permission. KMS and third-party libraries cannot decode it, and there is no such IAM API.
100: SSM Parameter Store holds secrets as SecureString values encrypted with KMS and EC2 instances read them using their IAM role, with very little administration. Storing secrets in S3 with signed URLs, instance metadata, or DynamoDB client-side encryption involves more custom work or is not designed for secrets.
101: A missing bucket is an API action recorded by AWS CloudTrail, so searching it for a DeleteBucket event shows who deleted the bucket and when. ELB logs, application logs and X-Ray do not record S3 management API calls, which makes them the wrong place to begin.
102: Running aws configure stores the developer's IAM access key ID and secret in the credentials file so the CLI signs requests with those permissions. Passing keys as parameters on each command is unsafe and not supported, user names and passwords are not used by the CLI, and a role needs credentials first.
103: Lambda scales out by running multiple concurrent execution environments to handle parallel S3 event invocations, up to the concurrency limit. It does not process requests sequentially, batch multiple images per invocation, or add compute per execution automatically.
104: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is an in-memory cache in front of DynamoDB that gives microsecond read latency and absorbs read spikes, so read capacity no longer needs over-provisioning. GSIs, S3 with Transfer Acceleration or retries do not reduce read latency to that level.
105: Lambda writes logs to CloudWatch Logs using its execution role, so if that role lacks permissions such as logs:CreateLogGroup, CreateLogStream and PutLogEvents, no log data appears. Lambda sends output automatically and creates the log group itself, and no source trigger is needed.
106: Traces from the app go to the local X-Ray daemon, which forwards them to X-Ray, so a missing daemon on the EC2 instance means no traces. The instance role also needs xray:PutTraceSegments and PutTelemetryRecords to send them. Read permissions like BatchGetTraces are for viewing.
107: Cognito developer-authenticated identities let your own backend authenticate users and map each user to one Cognito identity ID regardless of device. IAM user IDs or access keys are not meant for app end users, and a custom DynamoDB table does not give a managed identity or credentials.
108: aws cloudformation package uploads local artifacts to S3 and outputs a transformed template, and aws cloudformation deploy creates and executes the change set to launch the serverless application. The other combinations do not package local code or are not used for SAM deployment.

118: Cognito identity pools give authenticated and unauthenticated roles for registered and guest users with temporary credentials, and the application can alternatively use STS AssumeRole with a role for each user type. 151: An S3 event notification can invoke a Lambda function directly as soon as an object arrives, so you pay only for roughly ten short invocations per day with minimal latency. On-demand mode is ruled out by the requirement, and 10/2 is too low while 300/400 is overprovisioned.

160: Adding a read replica spreads read load and gives a failover target, because ElastiCache for Redis with replication can promote the replica if the primary fails. 161: AWS X-Ray traces requests as they flow through many microservices, builds a service map and shows latency and errors per component, which isolates the faulty service in a deep call stack. VPC Flow Logs show network traffic, GuardDuty detects threats, and Macie discovers sensitive data in S3.

237: A large Scan can consume a table's capacity in bursts, so use a smaller page size (limit) and let the Scan return fewer items per request, which spreads the load. Parallel scans increase consumption, and range indexes or updating items do not help.
238: To protect data at rest on EBS, you encrypt with an encrypted file system on top of the volume (or use EBS encryption). SSL does not encrypt at rest, S3 SSE does not apply to EBS, and IAM policies limit access but do not encrypt data.
239: If no Region is configured, the AWS SDKs use us-east-1 (N. Virginia) as the default for API calls. Other Regions require explicit configuration, and us-central-1 is not a valid Region.
240: SWF assigns tasks once and never duplicates them, executions can run up to a year, and workflows use deciders and workers to complete tasks. SWF does not need an S3 bucket or EC2 instances per domain, and it does not trigger SNS notifications on assignment.
241: The logs show the load tester hit only two servers in us-west-2a because it resolves the ELB DNS once and uses a single source IP, so requests concentrate on one ELB node. Re-resolving DNS per request or using distributed test clients spreads traffic across all ELB nodes and servers.
242: SNS delivers notifications over transports such as HTTP/HTTPS, email, SMS, SQS, Lambda and mobile push. UDP, DynamoDB and named pipes are not valid SNS delivery transports.
243: Storing large images in DynamoDB would consume lots of read and write capacity and exceeds the 400 KB item limit. Putting images in S3 and keeping only the S3 URL in the Product item adds almost no throughput load. DynamoDB has no foreign key constraints.
244: The number of tables per account and the provisioned throughput units per account are soft limits that AWS Support can raise. Items such as hash keys, local secondary indexes per table and storage are not limited in the way described.
245: Set an increased visibility timeout when retrieving the message so it stays hidden for the 5 minutes of processing, process it, then delete it after success. Deleting before processing risks losing the task, and DelaySeconds only delays the message becoming available.
246: A pre-signed URL gives time-limited access to a private object, so Company A generates one for each paying subscriber's request. An anonymous bucket policy exposes content to everyone, MFA is not practical for website visitors, and server-side encryption does not control who can download.
247: A good hash key has many distinct values with an even access pattern, such as User ID with many users, which spreads load across partitions. Keys with few values or one dominant value create hot partitions and waste provisioned throughput.
248: The query is by office and a name range, so the office identifier is the hash key and name is the range key, allowing a Query with a key condition on the range. Hashing on name or leaving out the range requires scanning more data and consumes more throughput.
249: EBS-backed instances can be stopped and restarted, preserving the root volume, while instance store-backed instances cannot be stopped (only rebooted or terminated). VPC and Auto Scaling do not require EBS-backed instances.
250: Auto Scaling and CloudFormation have no additional charge; you pay only for the resources they create. S3, EC2, Elastic Load Balancing and SWF are billed services.
251: S3 single PUT uploads are limited to 5 GB, but objects can be up to 5 TB using the multipart upload API, so use multipart for a 6 GB file. There is no large object API and support cannot raise the limit; the region does not matter.
252: Elastic Beanstalk can provision Auto Scaling groups, Elastic Load Balancers and RDS instances as part of an environment. It does not deploy Route 53 hosted zones, Elastic IP addresses or SQS queues as environment resources.
253: Use web identity federation: the app signs users in through Facebook and exchanges the token for temporary AWS security credentials (with Cognito or STS) to sign DynamoDB requests. Embedding IAM user or root credentials in a mobile app is insecure, and cross-account access does not apply.
254: AWS officially provides SDKs for languages such as Java, PHP, Python, .NET, Ruby, JavaScript, Go and C++. Perl, Pascal and SQL do not have officially supported AWS SDKs.
255: 600 gauges write one sample per minute, which is 600 / 60 = 10 writes per second. Each 1 KB write consumes 1 WCU, so 10 WCUs are required. The other values result from miscalculating the time unit.
256: DynamoDB returns 4xx HTTP status codes for problems with the client request, such as validation errors or throttling. 5xx codes indicate server-side problems, and 200 is success.
257: Setting ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds on the queue enables long polling, which waits up to 20 seconds for a message and reduces empty responses and CPU use. Visibility timeout, retention period and DelaySeconds do not affect how long a receive call waits.
258: S3 website endpoints use the format bucket-name.s3-website-region.amazonaws.com, so for Tokyo it is myawsbucket.s3-website-ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com. The other options are not valid S3 website endpoint formats.
259: Since items are only needed for an hour, create a table per hour and delete the table after analysis. Deleting a table is a single call and releases throughput and storage, while deleting items individually consumes write capacity and API calls, and retaining them costs storage.
260: Users are logged out because session state is stored on individual instances behind the load balancer. Storing session state in ElastiCache, a shared external store, lets any server read the session. Instance memory, instance storage and EBS are local, and Glacier is archival storage.
261: Removing public read access and serving photos through pre-signed URLs with an expiry means other sites can only hotlink links that soon stop working, while your own pages generate fresh URLs. EBS storage on a web server does not stop hotlinking and scales poorly. CloudFront alone still serves public content to anyone. Blocking IPs in security groups is impractical because hotlinking requests come from visitors' browsers, not from the offending servers.
262: DynamoDB does not lock items for reads or writes. It uses optimistic concurrency control, where conditional writes (for example, a condition expression on a version attribute) succeed only if the item is still in the expected state, otherwise the write fails and the client retries. Pessimistic locking and restricting item access during reads or writes describe traditional locking databases, not DynamoDB.
263: In SNS Mobile Push, each device token must be registered as a platform endpoint by calling the CreatePlatformEndpoint API against a platform application, and the app or a backend does this when the token is received. The console has no bulk CSV upload for device tokens. The push service only issues tokens and does not register them in SNS. A token vending service is unrelated, since it vends AWS credentials, not SNS endpoints.
264: DynamoDB divides provisioned throughput across partitions, and the partition key (hash key) decides which partition an item lands on. If requests concentrate on one hot partition key, that partition is throttled with ProvisionedThroughputExceededException even though table-wide consumption in CloudWatch looks below the limit. DynamoDB is serverless, so there are no storage instances, and a sort or range key does not define a partition by itself.
265: S3 historically partitioned index keys by key prefix, so keys that start with an evenly distributed, non-sequential value such as an instance ID spread load across partitions. Sequential or date-leading prefixes (HH-DD-MM, YYYY-MM-DD) concentrate requests on one partition and hurt performance. Today S3 scales per prefix automatically, but among these options the instance ID prefix is still the best choice.
266: Standard SQS queues give at-least-once delivery, so a message may be delivered more than once, and ordering is best-effort, meaning the order is not guaranteed. Consumers must be idempotent. Exactly-once processing with strict first-in first-out order is only offered by FIFO queues, which is not what these options describe for standard SQS.
267: Both correct options exchange LDAP-authenticated identity for temporary credentials from STS: the app authenticates against LDAP, then uses AssumeRole on a per-user role, or an identity broker calls STS (GetFederationToken) to return scoped federated credentials. IAM and STS cannot authenticate LDAP credentials directly, so the options where the app logs into IAM or STS with LDAP credentials fail. The broker must authenticate against LDAP, not against STS.
268: Static website hosting serves whatever object is named in the Index Document setting. To return welcome.html at the root, upload welcome.html to the bucket and change the Index Document property to welcome.html. Subfolders do not change the root document, and the Error Document is only returned for errors such as 404, not for normal requests.
269: Amazon S3 server-side encryption (SSE-S3, SSE-KMS and SSE-C) uses AES-256, the Advanced Encryption Standard block cipher. Triple DES, Blowfish and RC5 are not used by S3 for server-side encryption.
270: X-Ray annotations are key-value pairs added to the segment document that are indexed, so you can use them in filter expressions and groups to search traces. Metadata is also added to segments but is not indexed and cannot be used for filtering. Environment variables and SDK plugins configure the SDK and daemon but do not add custom indexed data.
271: An Elastic Beanstalk environment cannot change its load balancer type in place from Classic to Application. The supported migration is to create a new environment with the same configuration but an ALB, deploy the same application version, then swap CNAMEs for a cutover with little downtime. Editing, rebuilding or redeploying the existing environment does not change its load balancer type, and cloning copies the existing load balancer type.
272: AWS CodeCommit is a managed Git service, providing version control with commits of changes across multiple files, branching and history tracking. CodePipeline orchestrates release pipelines, CodeBuild compiles and tests code, and S3 is object storage with only basic object versioning, not branching or multi-file commits.
273: AWS CodeDeploy automates application deployments to EC2 instances, on-premises servers, Lambda and ECS. CodePipeline orchestrates stages but does not itself deploy to servers, CodeBuild builds and tests code, and Elastic Beanstalk deploys to AWS-managed environments, not to on-premises servers.
274: At 50 requests per second with 100 second executions, the function needs about 5000 concurrent executions. A new account has a default regional concurrency limit of 1000 (often lower), so the Developer must request a limit increase through AWS Support before deploying or invocations will be throttled. Dead-letter queues, an API Gateway trigger and code-level error handling do not raise the concurrency ceiling.
275: ElastiCache is an in-memory store with sub-millisecond latency, which gives the lowest latency for externalized session state and lets the web tier stay stateless. RDS and shared file systems are slower, and DynamoDB, while fast, has single-digit millisecond latency, which is higher than an in-memory cache.
276: A GSI has its own provisioned write capacity, and every write to the base table is also propagated to the GSI. If the GSI is under-provisioned, it throttles and back-pressures writes to the base table even when the base table has spare capacity. Read capacity, streams and activity on other tables do not cause this write throttling.
277: Conditional writes let an update succeed only if the item still has the expected state (for example, the price or a version attribute is unchanged), so a second editor's write fails instead of silently overwriting the first. This is optimistic locking. Concurrent writes is exactly the problem, atomic writes cover counters, and batch writes just group requests without protecting against overwrites.
278: Enabling a DynamoDB stream only produces the change records. Lambda must be wired to the stream with an event source mapping, which polls the stream and invokes the function. The stream view type only affects record contents, SNS cannot be mapped to a stream directly, and a longer timeout does not create the trigger.
279: Standard-resolution CloudWatch metrics have a minimum period of 60 seconds, so they cannot support scaling on the last 15 seconds. High-resolution custom metrics support periods down to 1 second, but data must be published often enough, so publishing every 5 seconds provides several data points within the 15 second window. Publishing every 30 seconds would leave windows with no data.
280: Kinesis Data Streams is built for ingesting very high volumes of streaming data from many producers, scales by shards for variable load, and enables real-time consumers such as fraud detection and dashboards via the KCL. SQS with EC2, S3 with Redshift, and Data Pipeline are batch or queue oriented and do not give real-time stream processing at this scale.
281: Least privilege means granting only the specific actions needed, which here are codecommit:CreateBranch and codecommit:DeleteBranch. The wildcard options (Put*, Update*, codecommit:*) grant many additional unneeded permissions, and Update* and Put* also do not include DeleteBranch.
282: Parameter Store (SecureString) can hold the credentials encrypted with KMS, and AWS KMS provides the key used to encrypt and decrypt them, so nothing is stored in code and values can be changed without redeploying. ACM manages TLS certificates, Trusted Advisor gives account recommendations, and GuardDuty is threat detection, none of which store secrets.
283: CodeDeploy uses the appspec.yml file in the deployment package to define what to deploy and the lifecycle hooks (for Lambda, the function versions and alias traffic shifting). buildspec.yml is for CodeBuild, dockerrun.aws.json is for Elastic Beanstalk Docker, and .ebextensions config files customize Elastic Beanstalk.
284: KMS Encrypt can only encrypt up to 4 KB of data directly, so a 10 MB document needs envelope encryption. Call GenerateDataKey, which returns a plaintext data key and an encrypted copy. Use the plaintext key to encrypt the data locally, discard it, and store the encrypted key with the data. GenerateRandom does not produce a KMS-protected key, and the encrypted key alone cannot encrypt data.
285: IntegrationLatency measures the time between API Gateway sending a request to the backend and receiving the response, while Latency measures the total time from API Gateway receiving the request to returning the response. Comparing the two shows whether the delay or timeout comes from the integration or from API Gateway itself. Cache hit and miss counts and Count do not show where time is spent.
286: CloudFront with signed URLs in front of S3 gives global low-latency delivery with controlled, time-limited access, and it is a single shared distribution so it is inexpensive. A distribution per customer is costly and hard to manage, Lambda@Edge adds cost and code, and API Gateway with Lambda in front of S3 adds more cost and has payload limits.
287: When the code cannot use the AWS SDK, which has built-in retries, the application should implement retries with exponential backoff itself to handle throttling errors. SQS, API Gateway and Kinesis Data Firehose add complexity and do not address the throttling at the DynamoDB API call level directly.
288: Session state should be externalized to a shared, fast, highly available in-memory store, and ElastiCache provides that so any instance can serve any user. CloudFront is a CDN and not a session store, S3 is too slow for session data, and sticky sessions tie users to one instance, which is lost if it fails.
289: The AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM) is an extension of CloudFormation that offers simplified syntax such as AWS::Serverless::Function, Api and SimpleTable for serverless resources, and is transformed into full CloudFormation. The other names are not real tools for this purpose.
290: To make a stateful server elastic, externalize state by storing session data in DynamoDB so any instance can serve any request, and put instances behind an ELB with an Auto Scaling group so capacity scales out and in. Pessimistic concurrency, CloudFront with a WAF, and CloudFront with Auto Scaling do not remove the state dependency or provide elasticity.
291: AWS X-Ray traces requests across distributed Lambda functions and downstream calls, producing a service map with segments, latency and errors, which lets you locate the root cause of performance problems in production. CloudWatch logs show only individual function output, CloudTrail records API calls, and Inspector assesses vulnerabilities, not performance.
292: A CloudWatch Logs metric filter only evaluates log events that are ingested after the filter is created, and it does not process existing historical data. So no data points appear for earlier exceptions. The other options describe requirements that do not exist, such as exporting to S3 or Elasticsearch.
293: A CloudFormation template that uses SAM resources must include the Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31 section at the root, which tells CloudFormation to expand SAM syntax into standard resources. Conditions, Globals and Properties are not the required marker, although Globals is an optional SAM section.
294: ElastiCache provides an in-memory cache (Redis or Memcached) that can hold results of repeated read queries so the application avoids hitting RDS, which reduces latency and database load. Multi-AZ gives availability, not read performance, SQS is messaging, and a read replica offloads reads but is not an in-memory cache.
295: When the second Lambda function consumes all of the account's concurrency, other functions, including the one behind /MyAPI, get throttled. Setting reserved concurrency on the second function limits how much it can use and guarantees the rest of the pool for others. Lowering the account limit or API Gateway throttling makes it worse, and sharding stages does not change Lambda concurrency.
296: Session data should be moved out of web server memory into an external, highly available store such as ElastiCache for Redis, which supports replication and failover, so any server can read the sessions and none are lost when a server fails. EBS volumes, the server's disk and a single dedicated EC2 instance are tied to one machine or are single points of failure.
297: Elastic Beanstalk only processes configuration files in the .ebextensions folder whose names end in .config (YAML or JSON format). A file named healthcheckurl.yaml is ignored, so it must be renamed healthcheckurl.config. The format is already valid, option_settings is the right section, and the namespace is a standard Elastic Beanstalk one.
298: Lambda does not let you choose CPU directly. You allocate memory, and CPU power, network bandwidth and other resources scale proportionally with it, so increasing memory speeds up compute-bound work. Raising the timeout only allows longer runs, and there are no instance sizes or invocation-time compute parameters.
299: Caching frequently accessed user data in ElastiCache for Memcached reduces repeated slow database reads during login, and calling the database asynchronously prevents the page from blocking while waiting on the query. A Lambda login function and an ALB do not reduce database wait time, and batching logins into one read is not practical and adds delay.
300: Amazon Cognito Sync stores user profile data in the cloud tied to an identity and synchronizes it across all devices of that identity, pushing updates through silent push notifications, with no backend to manage. Federated identities provide credentials, user pools handle sign-in, and Cognito events are triggers on sync actions, not a data store. Note that Cognito Sync is now superseded by AppSync.
301: With API Gateway native API key validation, a key is only usable if it is associated with a usage plan that includes the API stage. After CreateApiKey, the code must call CreateUsagePlanKey to link the key to the usage plan, otherwise the key is rejected with 403 Forbidden. Redeploying, authorizers and importing keys do not attach the key to a plan.
302: Amazon Cognito with web identity federation lets users sign in with Amazon, Facebook or Google and exchanges the token for temporary AWS credentials to access S3. SAML federation is for enterprise identity providers, and embedding access keys or calling AssumeRole from the app exposes long-term credentials or cannot authenticate public identities.
303: To make application log data from an EC2 instance available in CloudWatch, install and configure the CloudWatch Logs agent (or the unified CloudWatch agent) on the instance so it ships log files to CloudWatch Logs. GetMetricData reads metrics only, CloudTrail records API activity, and a new instance with CloudWatch Events does not collect existing application logs.
304: Deleting a table and recreating it is the fastest and cheapest way to empty a table with 1 million items, since deletes of individual items consume write capacity. DeleteItem loops, BatchWriteItem and scan-and-delete are slow and consume lots of write capacity units.
305: Asynchronous Lambda invocations from S3 are retried when the function returns an error or is throttled, with a delay between attempts. Retries use the same request ID, which explains duplicate log entries with the same ID. A wrong bucket name, an S3 outage or an application stop would not produce repeated invocations with the same request ID.
306: Amazon API Gateway provides a single, managed front door for many backend services, handling routing, authentication, throttling and versioning, so consumers use one interface. Lambda is compute, X-Ray is tracing and SQS is messaging, none of which unify access to multiple services.
307: A serverless static website with HTML, images, videos and JavaScript can be hosted in S3 and delivered globally with CloudFront. EC2, ECS with Redis, and Lambda with API Gateway require servers or are for dynamic APIs, not for serving static content.
308: Publish each application's key metric to a custom CloudWatch namespace, each with a unique metric name, then add those metrics to one dashboard for a single-screen view. Dimensions refine a metric, events are for state changes, and alarms alert on thresholds but do not provide a graphical overview.
309: Cognito user pools manage users, sign-up and sign-in and support self-service password reset, while identity pools exchange user pool tokens for temporary AWS credentials with IAM roles for authorization to AWS services. Using only identity pools with STS or IAM lacks a user directory, and KMS is unrelated.
310: CodeDeploy deployment groups represent separate target environments, so you can create groups for Development, QA and Production and deploy to them in sequence. CodeCommit is source storage, CodeBuild builds code, and Data Pipeline moves data, so none of those provide environment-staged deployments.
311: A date-based partition key causes a hot partition as all writes land on today's date, so throttling happens below provisioned capacity. Adding a random suffix to the partition key (write sharding) spreads writes across partitions at no extra cost. Raising capacity costs more and does not fix the hot key, and a table per date or a GSI do not fix the key distribution.
312: An in-memory store such as ElastiCache (Redis) provides a shared, central cache that all auto scaled instances can read and update with very fast performance and consistent accumulated results. S3, RDS and Kinesis are either slower or not designed for low-latency accumulated counters.
313: Elastic Beanstalk multi-container Docker environments use Amazon ECS to coordinate containers, and the containers are defined in a task definition file (Dockerrun.aws.json v2). A cluster is created by Elastic Beanstalk for you, and a Dockerfile is for single-container environments.
314: An EC2 instance profile attaches an IAM role to the instance, so the application gets automatically rotated temporary credentials through the instance metadata service, with no keys to store or manage. KMS and CodeCommit are not credential stores, and using the root user is highly insecure.
315: Pushing a count to CloudWatch as a custom metric is cheap, stores data points well past 10 days, and CloudWatch alarms can alert on thresholds with SNS notifications. RDS, X-Ray, or Kinesis with Lambda and DynamoDB add cost and complexity for something CloudWatch does natively.
316: Immutable deployments launch a full new set of instances in a separate Auto Scaling group and only switch over when they are healthy, so the live site stays available if the update fails, and rollback is quick by terminating the new instances. All at once causes downtime, rolling reduces capacity and rolls back slowly, and snapshots is not a deployment policy.
317: Placing ElastiCache in front of RDS caches repeatedly read items in memory so most reads never reach the database, reducing load during spikes. S3 is not a query cache, CloudFront custom origin for RDS is not possible, and local EC2 caches are not shared and are inefficient.
318: A strongly consistent read of up to 4 KB uses 1 RCU, so a 7 KB item needs 2 RCUs, and 3 items per second needs 6 RCUs. Writes use 1 KB units, so a 7 KB item needs 7 WCUs and 10 items per second needs 70 WCUs.
319: When a Lambda function reading a Kinesis stream returns an error, Lambda retries the batch until it succeeds or the data expires, and records that were already processed in the failed batch are processed again, creating duplicates. The function should handle the missing field gracefully instead of failing. Kinesis event sources are not asynchronous, and the stream pointer only advances after success.
320: Parameter Store SecureString parameters are encrypted with KMS and fetched by the application at runtime using its IAM role, so values can be updated or rotated without any code changes. Hard-coding secrets, storing them in S3 metadata, or relying only on an instance role does not provide secret storage and rotation.
321: Uploading a new ZIP to S3 does not change the deployed function, since Lambda copies the code at deployment time. Calling the update-function-code API with the new S3 object redeploys the function code in place with minimal disruption. Creating another function, deleting files or creating an alias does not update the code in the existing function.
322: To reach RDS in the VPC, the function must be attached to the VPC, and for internet access it must run in a private subnet whose route table sends outbound traffic to a NAT gateway. Lambda in a public subnet does not get a public IP, so it cannot reach the internet, and NACL changes and environment variables do not provide internet access.
323: Lambda created by CloudFormation only changes when the stack is updated. If the S3 key and bucket stay the same, CloudFormation sees no change, so the Developer must update the stack with a changed S3Bucket, S3Key or S3ObjectVersion value to trigger the code update. Base64 encoding and execution role permissions are not the problem.
324: On ECS, run the X-Ray daemon as a sidecar container from a Docker image, instrument the application with the X-Ray SDK, and give the task an IAM task role permitting the daemon to send data to X-Ray. Installing the daemon on the EC2 instance or using the instance role is less appropriate for containers, and there is no step to register the application.
325: Turning on S3 default encryption (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS) for the bucket encrypts all new objects at rest. The ACL condition and SecureTransport condition address access control and encryption in transit, and RDS is a different service.
326: The Mappings section of a CloudFormation template holds static lookup tables, such as a Region to AMI ID map, which can be read with Fn::FindInMap using the AWS::Region pseudo parameter. Parameters need user input, Outputs export values, and Resources define resources.
327: Query is more efficient than Scan because it reads only items matching a key condition, and eventually consistent reads cost half the read capacity of strongly consistent reads. Strongly consistent reads are also not supported on global secondary indexes.
328: CloudFront serves cached copies until they expire, so to see updates immediately, invalidate the cached objects at the edge locations (or use versioned file names). Removing the origin, disabling the distribution or changing forwarding settings does not clear cached objects.
329: A Lambda function in CloudFormation can include code inline with the ZipFile property (for small code, in some runtimes) or reference a ZIP in S3 with S3Bucket and S3Key. CloudFormation cannot pull code directly from CodeCommit, from a ZIP uploaded to CloudFormation itself, or from a private Git repository.
330: Custom libraries must be included in the deployment package, so install them locally next to the function code and upload everything as a ZIP (or use layers). Lambda cannot reference libraries hosted on S3 at runtime, blueprints are templates, and the runtime cannot be modified.
331: Offloading TLS to the load balancer removes the encryption work from the CPU-constrained instances. Install the SSL certificate on the ELB and terminate SSL there, then talk to instances over HTTP. SSL pass-through and installing certificates on the EC2 instances keep the encryption load on the instances.
332: A Lambda deployment package must contain the function code plus all libraries not in the runtime, bundled in a ZIP. Lambda cannot install libraries at runtime from scripts, buildspec files are for CodeBuild, and LD_LIBRARY_PATH does not point to S3.
333: Storing sessions in DynamoDB keeps session data outside the instances, in a highly available, scalable store, so a failed instance does not lose any sessions. Sticky sessions keep data on the instance, SQS is not a session store, and connection draining only helps to finish in-flight requests when removing instances.
334: DynamoDB Streams captures item changes in the Accounts table in near real time, and a consumer (such as Lambda) can apply them to the Payments data store, giving a simple, decoupled and reliable approach. Glue ETL is batch, ElastiCache triggers do not exist, and Firehose is intended for delivering data to destinations like S3 and not for DynamoDB-to-DynamoDB synchronization.
335: AWS CodeCommit is a managed Git service. Git is a distributed version control system where each user has a full local repository, can work offline, and changes are exchanged peer-to-peer. Subversion is centralized, CodeBuild is a build service and CodeStar is a project tool, not a repository.
336: A CloudWatch Events (EventBridge) rule with a schedule expression such as rate(10 minutes) can invoke the Lambda function, with no servers to manage. A cron job on EC2 is not serverless, environment variables do not trigger a function, and SNS subscriptions have no timer.
337: A GSI with partition key sport_name and sort key score lets the Developer query all users for a sport sorted by score, to get the top performers efficiently. Querying or scanning the base table by user_id would scan everything, and a local secondary index must use the same partition key as the base table (user_id), so it cannot have sport_name as its partition key.
338: Amazon Cognito identity pools support unauthenticated (guest) identities and associate them with an IAM role with limited permissions, providing temporary AWS credentials without any login. Creating IAM users or credentials per user is complex and insecure, and an identity provider requires users to authenticate.
339: To decrypt SSE-KMS objects, the application role needs permission to use the key (kms:Decrypt), granted in the IAM policy of the EC2 instance role, and the KMS key policy must allow this, such as by enabling IAM policies to grant access to the key. Bucket policies, ACLs and Systems Manager parameters do not grant KMS key permissions.
340: An SQS delay queue hides new messages from consumers for a configurable delay (0 to 15 minutes) after they are added to the queue. Hiding after consumption is the visibility timeout, polling for a period is long polling, and preventing deletion is not a feature.
341: CodeCommit is a managed Git service in AWS. Developers push only incremental changes (git sends deltas), which reduces upload time, and the code can be deployed directly to Elastic Beanstalk with low administrative effort. S3 uploads send full bundles, and FTP or EC2-hosted repositories require servers to manage.
342: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed in-memory cache for DynamoDB that reduces read latency to microseconds for repeated reads, with no application redesign beyond using the DAX client. EMR, SQS and CloudFront are not caches for DynamoDB reads.
343: Client-side encryption with S3 and KMS encrypts the data before it leaves the application, so it is protected in transit and at rest, and KMS usage is logged by CloudTrail for audit. Server-side default encryption alone does not protect data before upload, Cognito handles authentication, and Lambda-based encryption is unnecessary.
344: With web identity federation, the AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity response contains temporary credentials, and calls signed with the returned AccessKeyId carry the permissions of the IAM principal that owns the key, which is the assumed role session. The role ID AROACLKWSDQRAOEXAMPLE is just an identifier in the response, and the other options are unrelated to the credentials.
345: The AWS CLI by default pages results, but listing large numbers of resources in one call can time out. Using pagination with smaller page sizes (for example, --page-size) makes multiple smaller API calls and avoids timeouts. Shorthand syntax, parameter values and quoting strings only affect how commands are written.
346: Port mappings, which map container ports to host ports, are defined in the container definition section of an ECS task definition. Security groups, ECR and the container agent do not define port mappings.
347: DynamoDB provides single-digit millisecond latency, which makes it a good index for S3 object metadata that a web application queries. EC2 and Lambda are compute, and RDS is a relational database that does not provide the same latency characteristics at scale.
348: CloudWatch Logs is the managed service for centralizing and securely storing application and system logs from EC2, with retention and encryption options. VPC Flow Logs capture network traffic, CloudSearch is a search service, and CloudTrail records API calls.
349: When a Kinesis stream cannot keep up, throughput is limited by the number of shards, each supporting 1 MB or 1000 records per second for writes. Increasing the shard count with UpdateShardCount adds capacity. KPL and PutRecords improve producer efficiency but do not add capacity, and reducing retention does not increase ingestion.
350: Nested stacks let you reuse common template patterns, such as a load balancer or security group configuration, as separate templates, breaking a large template into manageable pieces. Embedding credentials is insecure, removing mappings does not help maintainability, and AWS::Include is a macro-based snippet include, not the best practice for this.
351: Throttling or limit errors from AWS APIs should be handled by retrying with exponential backoff, so the application slows its request rate and retries successfully. Load balancing the app, moving it to EC2, or adding a fixed one second delay does not address bursts adaptively.
